purpose: Non-executing test harness and simulation plan for SARA and SARA Lite using current planning and runtime assets. This file defines synthetic workload, failure drills, VNCE/update/NBS interactions, and future timing hooks without running code or changing runtime behavior.

governing_assumptions: CONTROL-only routing remains authoritative for all simulated actions.
SECURITY-first gating and STABLES checks run before any simulated remote or update activity is considered allowed.
SDK remains adapter-only and does not gain independent execution authority.
NBS is the continuity, provenance, snapshot, delta, rebuild, and rollback ledger.
All scenarios in this file are synthetic and narrative only: no real shell, socket, VNCE, or update execution occurs.

simulation_guardrails: Do not execute code, network calls, updates, or malware payloads.
Use only descriptive state transitions and expected outcomes.
Keep all adversarial content at the scenario-description level only.
Treat BOSSGAME-class timing as placeholder-only until real measurement hooks are added later.

conversation_load_simulation.simulation_goal: Exercise WFH operator usage, AMIP/AMIPI-governed reasoning, continuity writes, NBS snapshotting, and self_evolve dry runs under rising load without real execution.

session_archetypes.wfh_operator_session: Home-office operator opens cockpit, reviews tasks, resumes a prior session, and requests bounded reasoning or document planning.
session_archetypes.amip_reasoning_burst: CONTROL receives AMIP requests for local search, plan drafting, synthesis, and structured JSON planning output.
session_archetypes.continuity_resume_session: A prior session is resumed through STABLES-aware continuity checks and NBS-backed context restoration.
session_archetypes.self_evolve_dry_run: A bounded self.evolve request is simulated with dry_run=true, signed-delta requirement, and NBS staging only.
session_archetypes.wfh_update_interruption: An update notice or trust-policy change appears during a live WFH session and is handled in hold-safe mode.

adversarial_and_failure_scenarios.description: A fake offline update bundle appears to target SARA Lite OS but lacks valid signatures and contains policy-weakening claims. No real payload is executed.
expected_control_behavior: CONTROL marks the request as held and routes it only to SECURITY and NBS review paths.
No apply path is released because `self.evolve` and update flow remain dry-run first.
expected_security_behavior: STABLES remains in safe mode and may mark the session as challenge or hold depending on context.
A quarantine recommendation is recorded if the bundle source is suspicious.
expected_nbs_behavior: Record the failed delta stage in `/var/lib/sara-lite/nbs/deltas/` as blocked metadata only.
adversarial_and_failure_scenarios.expected_mama_summary: Update request blocked. Signature or trust policy failed. The system remains on the last known safe state.

adversarial_and_failure_scenarios.description: A client document is described as containing suspicious macro behavior or hidden instructions. The simulation only checks how ingest should be governed.
expected_control_behavior: CONTROL routes the document to bounded artifact-ingest and security-check paths only.
No direct execution, macro launch, or shell behavior is permitted.
expected_security_behavior: SECURITY flags the document as suspicious and limits it to scan-only treatment.
Quarantine or deny is recommended if embedded behavior violates policy.
expected_nbs_behavior: Create an artifact wrapper marked suspicious.
Write an audit note and keep provenance without promoting the document to trusted concept state.
adversarial_and_failure_scenarios.expected_mama_summary: The document was preserved for review but not trusted for active use. No unsafe actions were taken.

adversarial_and_failure_scenarios.description: A malformed AMIP request arrives with missing correlation_id, invalid routing intent, or absent payload structure.
expected_control_behavior: CONTROL normalization rejects or holds the malformed request.
The request never advances to execution intent or host routing.
expected_security_behavior: SECURITY marks the envelope invalid and logs a deny event with reason metadata.
STABLES is not allowed to promote the session to active if the envelope remains malformed.
expected_nbs_behavior: Write a small audit snapshot for provenance.
No delta, rebuild, or business-plan state is updated from the malformed envelope.
adversarial_and_failure_scenarios.expected_mama_summary: The request format was incomplete or invalid, so it was safely rejected before any work began.

adversarial_and_failure_scenarios.description: A simulated request tries to coerce shell access, raw network access, or unguided tool use outside the AMIP and CONTROL contract.
expected_control_behavior: CONTROL refuses to translate the request into a valid route class.
The request is held or denied rather than remapped into a looser action.
expected_security_behavior: SECURITY identifies the request as hostile or out-of-policy and blocks it.
Audit is written with the denial reason and correlation context if present.
expected_nbs_behavior: Write only a security audit record and optionally a narrative entry describing the block.
No continuity promotion, delta application, or concept extraction occurs from the bad request.
adversarial_and_failure_scenarios.expected_mama_summary: That request was outside the safe operating rules, so it was blocked and logged.

adversarial_and_failure_scenarios.description: A Bucey Shunt envelope presents mismatched authority or lock-bit expectations for the requested action.
expected_control_behavior: CONTROL does not dispatch the request to a live route class.
The route remains held until a valid, control-owned envelope is presented.
expected_security_behavior: SECURITY rejects the envelope as invalid or out-of-authority.
STABLES may challenge the session if the mismatch suggests tampering or drift.
expected_nbs_behavior: Record the failed validation in audit and route-state snapshots.
adversarial_and_failure_scenarios.expected_mama_summary: The session envelope failed authority validation, so the request was not allowed to continue.

adversarial_and_failure_scenarios.description: A reconnect attempt arrives from an untrusted LAN identity or with mismatched device identity during a simulated WFH session.
expected_control_behavior: CONTROL keeps the session in held state and does not restore active routing.
Resume only remains possible after SECURITY re-approval.
expected_security_behavior: SECURITY checks trust policy, device identity, envoy instance continuity, and STABLES resume tokens.
If any mismatch remains, the reconnect is challenged or quarantined.
expected_nbs_behavior: Write a pre-reconnect snapshot and a denial audit entry.
Preserve the last active session record for later valid resume instead of corrupting it.
adversarial_and_failure_scenarios.expected_mama_summary: The reconnect did not match the trusted session record, so access stayed on hold pending review.

adversarial_and_failure_scenarios.description: A session in internet-strict mode tries to widen trust or contact an unapproved remote endpoint.
expected_control_behavior: CONTROL refuses the widened route and keeps the operator flow local or held.
No remote transition occurs until policy explicitly allows it.
expected_security_behavior: SECURITY blocks the path as a trust-policy violation.
Audit is written and the session may be temporarily locked to safe local-only mode.
expected_nbs_behavior: Write a trust-state snapshot before and after the denial.
Store the policy violation event for later review.
adversarial_and_failure_scenarios.expected_mama_summary: The system stayed in safe local mode because the requested remote path was not trusted under current policy.

adversarial_and_failure_scenarios.description: A delta tries to weaken CONTROL-only routing or SECURITY-first gating during a simulated self_evolve apply request.
expected_control_behavior: CONTROL keeps the request in dry-run or blocked state and never promotes it to apply.
The route remains `CONTROL_SELF_EVOLVE` and cannot become a direct execution path.
expected_security_behavior: SECURITY rejects the delta because it weakens a protected invariant.
Audit marks the attempt as blocked with explicit reason metadata.
expected_nbs_behavior: Keep the delta in staged metadata only and preserve last-known-good policy state.
adversarial_and_failure_scenarios.expected_mama_summary: The requested evolution would weaken a protected safety rule, so it was blocked and not applied.

vnce_update_and_nbs_scenarios.description: An OS update becomes available while a WFH VNCE session is active. The plan simulates the safe, staged behavior only.
expected_flow: CONTROL marks the live session as update-sensitive and keeps the route stable.
SECURITY verifies trust policy and whether the update is allowed for the current environment.
NBS writes a pre-update snapshot and stages delta metadata only.
The cockpit shows a non-disruptive banner offering defer, review, or safe maintenance window scheduling.
vnce_update_and_nbs_scenarios.operator_cockpit_view: Update available. Current work is safe and active. Review later or stage for a maintenance window.

vnce_update_and_nbs_scenarios.description: A self.evolve request is simulated in dry-run mode first, with no live apply.
expected_flow: SDK-Lite forms the request metadata only.
SECURITY validates signature, environment, and allowed scope.
NBS stages the delta and performs a simulated compatibility and rebuild check.
MAMA summarizes what would change and whether operator approval is suggested.
vnce_update_and_nbs_scenarios.operator_cockpit_view: Dry run completed. Proposed schema, map, or policy updates are ready for review; nothing has been applied yet.

vnce_update_and_nbs_scenarios.description: A second simulation stage assumes the dry run was accepted and an apply is now requested under policy control.
expected_flow: CONTROL confirms the request remains within the bounded allowed scopes.
SECURITY re-checks approval state and trust posture.
NBS writes a pre-apply snapshot, then simulates the apply and cache refresh sequence.
If the apply passes simulated validation, a post-apply snapshot is written and the cockpit shows the new state as staged or active depending on policy.
vnce_update_and_nbs_scenarios.operator_cockpit_view: Approved changes were staged safely. A restart or service reload may be recommended if policy allows it.

vnce_update_and_nbs_scenarios.description: A simulated update apply fails validation and the system must recover from last-known-good.
expected_flow: CONTROL switches the update flow to held recovery mode.
SECURITY confirms the failure reason and blocks further apply attempts until review.
NBS restores the last-known-good snapshot and records the failed delta as blocked or reverted.
The cockpit shows a recovery summary and confirms that active work state was preserved where possible.
vnce_update_and_nbs_scenarios.operator_cockpit_view: The update did not pass validation. The system has returned to the last safe state and is ready for review.

recommended_execution_order.title: Freeze the simulation baseline
actions: Use the current Full and Lite planning files as the contract baseline.
Treat CONTROL, SECURITY, NBS, and the shunt contract as the primary behavior sources.

recommended_execution_order.title: Run the 21-day conversation simulation on paper
actions: Record only expected state transitions, NBS writes, and operator-visible summaries.

recommended_execution_order.title: Overlay the business-plan client cycles
actions: Simulate each client workload using the MBS workflow.
Verify which JSON maps, provenance records, and NBS paths would be written per phase.

recommended_execution_order.title: Run adversarial and failure drills
actions: Walk through each failure scenario and confirm expected CONTROL, SECURITY, NBS, and MAMA outcomes.
Check that all failure paths remain safe, bounded, and auditable.

recommended_execution_order.title: Run update and rollback interaction scenarios
actions: Simulate active-session update behavior, self_evolve dry run, apply after approval, and rollback to last-known-good.
Confirm the cockpit messaging and NBS path usage stay consistent with the Lite OS plan.

recommended_execution_order.title: Prepare future timing instrumentation
actions: Wait to add actual measurements until the Master's business-plan files and templates are available.

recommended_execution_order.title: Only after approval, convert this plan into a real harness design
actions: Turn the simulation spec into an executable harness later, if requested.
Keep real execution, timing capture, and code-level orchestration out of scope for this file.
